newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close down, property stocks up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close down, property stocks up.

text.p: Singapore share prices closed slightly lower on Thursday in aimless trade with foreign shares sold down, dealers said.

The foreign shares of Singapore Press Holdings, UOB and DBS banks, and Singapore Airlines were among the top losers for the day. The new Business Times Singapore Regional Index (SRI) closed down 6.92 points, or 0.70 percent, to 976.30 points.
"There was no follow through buying from yesterday," one dealer with a foreign brokerage house said.
The Straits Times Industrial Index closed down 2.54 points to 2,068.72 points.
Property shares led the gainers for the day with the index up 1.07 percent, or 6.71 points, to 634.69 points.

Dealers said trading was more active on the Malaysian second board which spilled over to the Malaysian shares traded over the counter in Singapore. The UOB OTC index was up 4.69 points to 1,190.95 points.
Debut share CM Telecom closed up at US$0.30, down marginally from its initial offer price of $0.32, with 9.77 million shares traded.
Total volume reached 92.80 million shares with losers outpacing gainers 164 to 143. -- Raj Rajendran (+65-870-3093)
